items.title: The Disappearing Heap
items.question: A heap minus one grain stays a heap — yet repeated removals leave bare floor. Refusing any single step as the turning point, what follows?
items.correctExplanation: Paradox undeniable — each tolerance step compels, yet floors aren't heaps. Valid-seeming marches end absurdly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is paradox: undeniable steps, impossible end. Floors don't vanish and logic doesn't forbid grains: tolerance plus iteration yields contradiction. Steps compel; destinations appall.
items.lessonContent:
Steps compel; destinations appall reliably.
Tolerance plus iteration breeds paradox.
Undeniable premises, impossible conclusions.
Marches mislead one grain at a time.
Share this: remove one grain mentally.

items.title: The Tolerant Step
items.question: Sorites arguments run on a tolerance principle: tiny differences never flip category membership. What does tolerance license?
items.correctExplanation: Step marches to absurdity — tolerance makes each move safe and the journey impossible. Local safety, global disaster.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is step-by-step marches to absurdity. Skipping, ignoring, and volume miss it: tolerance blesses every footstep toward cliffs. Locally safe composes globally absurd.
items.lessonContent:
Locally safe composes globally absurd.
Footsteps blessed march toward cliffs.
Tolerance licenses treks, never jumps.
Safety per step hides journey peril.
Share this: bless one small step.

items.title: The Receding Hairline
items.question: Losing one hair never makes anyone bald — yet bald heads exist in mirrors everywhere. What mirrors the heap exactly?
items.correctExplanation: Baldness sorites — hair-by-hair tolerance marches to shining crowns. Mirrors confirm what logic denies.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is baldness sorites. Transplants, chemistry, and fashion miss it: one-hair tolerance iterates into baldness. Crowns shine where steps compelled.
items.lessonContent:
Hair-by-hair tolerance marches onward.
Crowns shine where steps compelled.
Mirrors confirm logic's denials false.
Marches end on bare scalps.
Share this: lose one hair hypothetically.

items.title: The Dollar Line
items.question: Poverty lines declare $X poor, $X+1 not — a cent manufacturing prosperity. What does the line reveal?
items.correctExplanation: Stipulation, not discovery — lines drawn for administration, not found in nature. Cents don't create prosperity.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is stipulation, not discovery. Truth, revelation, and magic miss it: thresholds serve bureaucracy, never metaphysics. Drawn lines administer; they never discern.
items.lessonContent:
Thresholds administer; they never discern.
Cents manufacture nothing real ever.
Drawn lines serve bureaucracies solely.
Stipulation poses as discovery daily.

items.title: The Moved Definition
items.question: Death was cardiac arrest for millennia; now brain criteria decide, partly to serve transplants. What does the shift show?
items.correctExplanation: Death's boundary partly stipulated — criteria track practices (transplant needs) as well as biology. Definitions serve as well as describe.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is death's boundary is partly stipulated. Murder, irrelevance, and souls miss it: cardiac-to-brain moves mixed discovery with decision. Boundaries serve practices too.
items.lessonContent:
Definitions serve as well as describe.
Criteria track practices partly always.
Boundaries mix discovery with decision.
Stipulation shares work with science.

items.title: The Birthday Majority
items.question: Voting at 18, drinking at 21, renting cars at 25 — maturity arrives by statute, differently per privilege. What are these ages?
items.correctExplanation: Legal stipulations — ages vary by jurisdiction and purpose: maturity has no birthday in nature. Statutes decide what brains blur.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is legal stipulations. Neurology, morals, and physics miss it: thresholds differ across borders and beverages. Administrations need lines; nature provides none.
items.lessonContent:
Administrations need lines nature lacks.
Thresholds vary by border and beverage.
Maturity has no birthday in nature.
Statutes decide what brains blur.

items.title: The Circling Song
items.question: Greenish warblers ring Tibet: each population interbreeds with neighbors, but end populations cannot. What breaks in nature?
items.correctExplanation: The species concept — ring species make 'same species' intransitive: A=B, B=C, yet A≠C. Nature ignores our filing.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the species concept. Wings, routes, and colors miss it: interbreeding chains loop back incompatible. Filing systems fail where continua flow.
items.lessonContent:
Continua flow where filing fails.
Intransitivity breaks species logic.
Chains loop back incompatible fully.
Nature ignores human filing.

items.title: The Orange Border
items.question: Red shades into orange with no borderline in the spectrum — yet English insists on two color words. What lacks edges?
items.correctExplanation: Color terms' extensions — spectra flow continuously; words cut arbitrarily. Edges live in language, never light.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is color terms' extensions. Glass, bulbs, and tubes miss it: boundaries sit in vocabulary, not wavelengths. Continua defy dictionaries daily.
items.lessonContent:
Boundaries live in vocabulary solely.
Spectra flow; words cut arbitrarily.
Edges absent from light itself.
Continua defy dictionaries daily.

items.title: The Height Line
items.question: At what exact height does short become tall?
items.correctExplanation: No sharp cutoff — tallness lacks edges by nature: 179.9 vs 180.0 differ negligibly. Vagueness lives here.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no sharp cutoff exists. Centimeters, medians, and doctors miss it: predicates without borders admit no lines. Height varies; tallness vagaries persist.
items.lessonContent:
Predicates without borders admit no lines.
Centimeters vary; tallness vagaries persist.
Cutoffs invented, never discovered here.
Height flows; labels dam arbitrarily.

items.title: The Wealth Line
items.question: How many dollars make someone rich?
items.correctExplanation: No principled dollar — riches fade in gradually: millions differ by degree, never kind. Lines serve taxes, not truths.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is no principled dollar divides. Round millions pretend precision: no cent transforms pauper to prince. Gradual fortunes defy sharp coronations.
items.lessonContent:
Gradual fortunes defy sharp coronations.
Cents transform nothing essential ever.
Lines serve taxes, never truths.
Richness fades in by degrees.

items.title: The Fountain Verdict
items.question: Duchamp's urinal in a gallery: art or plumbing?
items.correctExplanation: Context confers status — galleries, intentions, histories make art, not porcelain. Essences absent; institutions present.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is context confers art status. Plumbing, vandalism, and weight miss it: placement plus theory transmute fixtures. Art lives in frames, never atoms.
items.lessonContent:
Frames transmute fixtures into art.
Institutions present what essences can't.
Placement plus theory perform magic.
Galleries author statuses daily.
Share this: frame one ordinary thing.

items.title: The Game Resemblance
items.question: Wittgenstein: games share no single essence, only overlapping similarities like family faces. What replaces definitions?
items.correctExplanation: Family resemblance — crisscrossing similarities without common cores: noses here, temperaments there. Essences retire; networks suffice.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is family resemblance. Dictionaries, rules, and pointing miss it: games hang together resemblantly, never essentially. Look, don't think, for essences.
items.lessonContent:
Networks suffice where essences retire.
Resemblances crisscross without cores.
Look-and-see beats define-and-fail.
Families share faces, never formulas.
Share this: resemble one game tonight.

items.title: The Unanimous Verdict
items.question: Supertrue means true on every admissible way of sharpening a vague term. What survives all precisifications?
items.correctExplanation: Supertruth — unanimity across sharpenings: borderline cases may vary, core truths persist. Precision-proof verdicts stand.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is supertruth. Volume, age, and brevity miss it: truth surviving every admissible sharpening earns the prefix. Cores persist; penumbras wobble.
items.lessonContent:
Cores persist; penumbras wobble always.
Unanimity across sharpenings decides.
Precision-proof verdicts stand firm.
Borders vary; centers hold fast.

items.title: The Secret Threshold
items.question: Williamson holds vague boundaries exist sharply but unknowably — some exact cent makes tallness, forever hidden. What is claimed?
items.correctExplanation: Unknowable sharp cutoffs — epistemicism: bivalence holds with ignorance guaranteed. Lines exist unseen by design.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is unknowable sharp cutoffs. Nothings, fuzzies, and magic miss it: margins of error hide exact borders necessarily. Ignorance is structural, not temporary.
items.lessonContent:
Ignorance structures vague domains.
Borders exist unseen by design.
Margins of error hide exactness.
Bivalence holds without witnesses.

items.title: The Graded Truth
items.question: Fuzzy logic assigns heapness 0.7 instead of plain true or false. What replaces bivalence?
items.correctExplanation: Graded truth — degrees between 0 and 1: heaps 0.7, baldness 0.3. Bivalence yields to spectra.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is graded truth values. Volume, anger, and length miss it: truth comes in degrees here. Spectra replace switches in vague domains.
items.lessonContent:
Spectra replace switches in vagueness.
Degrees quantify borderline standings.
Bivalence yields gracefully here.
Truth admits sevenths and thirds.

items.title: The Blurry Borderline
items.question: Borderline cases have borderline borderlines — 'definitely' gets vague too, endlessly. What regresses?
items.correctExplanation: Vagueness itself — higher-order vagueness: borderlines blur recursively. Definitely needs its own border patrol.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is vagueness itself. Counting, grammar, and spelling miss it: definitively-definite recedes forever. Orders ascend without terminating.
items.lessonContent:
Borders blur recursively always.
Definitely needs border patrol too.
Orders ascend without terminating.
Vagueness infects its own edges.

items.title: The March Diagnosis
items.question: The forced march compels each step while forbidding the destination. What is the standard shape of the puzzle?
items.correctExplanation: Valid-seeming steps, unacceptable end — puzzle shape: plausible moves composing impossible treks. Diagnosis precedes cure.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is valid-seeming steps, unacceptable end. Invalid-first, premise-less, and sound-true miss it: the puzzle's form is compelling-parts-absurd-whole. Shape recognized, solutions vary.
items.lessonContent:
Compelling parts compose absurd wholes.
Shape recognized precedes cures found.
Plausible moves mislead systematically.
Diagnosis maps puzzle anatomy.

items.title: The Reasonable Ghost
items.question: Law judges by the 'reasonable person' — a vague standard applied daily without precision. Why does law embrace vagueness?
items.correctExplanation: Vagueness enables contextual justice — reasonable persons adapt across cases rules cannot foresee. Flexibility needs blur.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is vagueness enables contextual justice. Laziness, billing, and naps miss it: precision would petrify judgment. Ghosts haunt courtrooms usefully.
items.lessonContent:
Flexibility needs blur to function.
Precision would petrify judgment fully.
Ghosts haunt courtrooms usefully.
Contextual justice needs vague vessels.

items.title: The Doubt Standard
items.question: 'Beyond reasonable doubt' convicts without numbers — roughly 90%? 95%? Deliberately unstated. What kind of standard is this?
items.correctExplanation: Moral certainty, unquantified — firm conviction without percentages: conscience calibrated, never computed. Numbers would cheapen verdicts.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is moral certainty, unquantified. Formulas, coins, and whims miss it: law demands settled minds, not tallied odds. Certainty moralized decides fates.
items.lessonContent:
Settled minds decide fates lawfully.
Numbers would cheapen verdicts badly.
Conscience calibrated, never computed.
Unquantified certainty convicts justly.

items.title: The Conscious Machine
items.question: If an AI claimed consciousness convincingly, no settled test could verify it — the hard problem has no meter. What is missing?
items.correctExplanation: Agreed criteria — consciousness lacks operational tests all accept: claims outrun verification permanently. Meters missing, debates permanent.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is agreed criteria. Chips, speakers, and data miss it: the hard problem yields no instrument. Convincing performances prove nothing settled.

Meters missing stall verdicts permanently.
Hard problems yield no instruments.
Criteria precede consciousness tests.

items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is continuous communication. Contracts, telepathy, and avoidance miss it: borderlines require dialogue, not documents. Checking respects ambiguity.

Gray zones demand ongoing talk.

items.title: The Disease Edge
items.question: Is aging a disease? Is grief? Medicine's categories blur at edges where treatment meets enhancement. What does this show?

items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is borderline cases exist. Ignorance, fraud, and myth miss it: nosology has penumbras like all vague kinds. Edges humble definers.

Edges blur honest categories.

Borderlines exist in medicine too.

Sluggish copying sits astride life.

Borderlines test biology best.

items.title: The Voted Planet
items.question: Pluto's 2006 demotion followed a vote on definitions, not new telescope data about Pluto itself. What demoted it?
items.correctExplanation: Stipulative redefinition — astronomers voted criteria (clearing orbit) Pluto fails: definitions demote, discoveries don't. Planets by ballot.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is stipulative redefinition. Size, drift, and cold miss it: Pluto unchanged, category moved. Ballots reclassify heavens regularly.

Planets elected, never discovered purely.

items.title: The Exact Heap
items.question: How many grains make a heap — exactly?
items.correctExplanation: No sharp number — heaps admit no exact threshold: vagueness all the way down. Questions outrun answers here.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no sharp number exists. Precise millions pretend precision vagueness forbids: countability differs from cutoffs. Grains count; heaps don't begin.

Grains count; heaps never begin sharply.

Questions outrun answers sometimes.
